title: GitHub Actions: test, build once, and promote an artifact
outcome: Design a CI/CD path with explicit permissions, artifact identity, and release gates.
drawbacks: Runner trust, secrets, caches, and release compatibility need design.

trace.title: Workflow trigger
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A workflow is triggered by an event and runs jobs/steps on runners. CI should produce relevant evidence for a change: type checks, tests, build, and selected integration checks.

CD promotes a known artifact into an environment under deliberate permissions.

Build once from a known revision and record the image digest. Do not rebuild independently for staging and production and call them the same tested artifact.

Cache dependencies for speed, but do not let a cache replace a lockfile or validation.

Choose narrow workflow permissions and supported temporary cloud identity where appropriate. Untrusted PR code must not receive powerful deployment secrets.

Pin third-party actions according to the team’s supply-chain policy and review their access.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
PR event → least-privilege test job → passing evidence → identified artifact → deliberate environment gate → deployment → smoke/monitor → rollback decision. Keep credentials scoped to jobs/environments that need them.

Treat migration compatibility and external effects as release concerns. A green CI job cannot make a destructive data rollback reversible.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A build from a dirty local tree is not the CI-tested revision. Broad write permissions on untrusted workflows widen access.

A deployment without a smoke check can be green while users fail.
